subject: Stakeholder mapping & procurement next steps - Acme Commerce
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme-commerce.com>, Jacob Lee <j.lee@acme-commerce.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra, vivek_kulkarni
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Stakeholder mapping & procurement next steps - Acme Commerce

Hi Emily,

Great to meet your team on the call today — thanks for walking through the use case and traffic profile. Quick recap and the things we discussed you said you'd share:

- Goal: evaluate Redwood for low-latency model inference across storefront personalization and search ranking.
- Initial scope: 5 production endpoints, burst QPS up to ~800, latency SLOs ~150ms p95.
- Decision timeline: you mentioned aiming for a vendor decision by end of Q2.

To help us map the right stakeholders and accelerate procurement, can you please: 
1) Share a simple org chart or list of decision-makers (economic buyer, primary product/engineering owner, security/infrastructure contact, legal/procurement).
2) Confirm the procurement/legal steps and any required contracting templates or PO process.
3) Confirm the security artifacts you'll need (SOC 2, pen test, security questionnaire) and the right point of contact.

From our side we will:
- Put together a security pack (SOC2 summary, questionnaire responses, architecture notes).
- Draft a mutual action plan with milestone dates and a recommended 60-90 day POC approach.
- Share a preliminary pricing range so procurement has something to evaluate.

Next steps: if you can reply with the stakeholder names/roles and preferred times for intros, I will schedule a short intro with our security lead and solutions engineer. Attaching a one-page draft MAP (no PII).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachment: draft-MAP-acme-1pager.pdf

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme-commerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jacob Lee <j.lee@acme-commerce.com>, Sarah Patel <s.patel@acme-commerce.com>, procurement@acme-commerce.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping & procurement next steps - Acme Commerce

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the draft MAP. Helpful. See the high-level stakeholder list below and I attached a simple org chart.

- Economic buyer: Michael Torres, VP Product (m.torres@acme-commerce.com) — will sign off on budget and vendor selection.
- Product/engineering owner: Rajiv Menon, Director, Search & Personalization (r.menon@acme-commerce.com) — primary technical sponsor.
- Security/infosec: Jacob Lee, Head of InfoSec (j.lee@acme-commerce.com) — will own the questionnaire and risk review.
- Legal: Sarah Patel, Senior Counsel (s.patel@acme-commerce.com) — handles contract redlines.
- Procurement: procurement@acme-commerce.com — standard PO process, net 30.

Timeline: target decision by 2026-06-30. Procurement needs a pricing range and SOW by early June to route budget.

Security asks: Jacob will need Redwood's SOC 2 report or SOC 2 summary and answers to our standard security questionnaire (I can send the form).

I attached an org chart: ACME-orgchart-v1.png. I'll loop Jacob and procurement on the next threads for the questionnaire.

Two quick Qs:
1) Can you confirm whether Redwood supports dedicated VPC/private deployments for data residency?
2) Can you share a rough price band for a 60-90 day POC for the scale we discussed?

Thanks,
Emily
Head of Product Partnerships | Acme Commerce
Attachment: ACME-orgchart-v1.png

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme-commerce.com>, Jacob Lee <j.lee@acme-commerce.com>, procurement@acme-commerce.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra, vivek_kulkarni
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping & procurement next steps - Acme Commerce

Emily — perfect, thanks for the names and the org chart. Answers below and proposed next steps.

1) VPC/private deployments: yes — Redwood offers Private deployments (VPC & on-prem options) and a dedicated capacity model. We will include an architecture note specific to your region and data residency requirements in the security pack.

2) Pricing band for a 60-90 day POC: 
   - Estimated range: $25k - $45k for a scoped POC covering the endpoints/scale we discussed (dedicated capacity with baseline throughput, reserve burst capacity). We'll provide a detailed SOW & pricing options (monthly reserved vs. POC short-term).

Proposed next steps:
- I will send our Redwood Security Pack (SOC2 summary, questionnaire responses, architecture notes) to Jacob.
- Can Jacob confirm the questionnaire format (docx vs. online) and a point person?
- Procurement — if you can share any template or procurement contact (name) I will route a preliminary SOW and pricing band for review.
- Suggest a 30-minute intro sync next week to align on the POC scope and acceptance criteria (latency SLOs, data handling, ramp plan).

Attachments: will include Redwood security pack in my next message (zipped).

If that works I'll schedule the intro and drop the security pack into the Drive link I shared earlier. What times next Wednesday or Thursday look good for you all?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachment (to follow): redwood-security-pack.zip

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
